scoring.check_status: Each check returns pass | warning | fail | na and a score between 0 and its weight.
scoring.conditional: A check with conditional: true may return na (not applicable). Its weight is then removed from the denominator, so a plain content site is scored out of max_score minus that weight.
scoring.unreachable: A check never scores a site down for a resource it could not read (network error, 401/403/429/503, timeout). It returns warning at roughly half weight with inconclusive: true.
scoring.percentage: round(total_score / available_points * 100), where available_points = max_score minus the weight of na checks.

checks.name: AI Bot Crawlability
checks.description: Parses the origin's robots.txt and tests, for each of the 126 AI crawler user-agent tokens in the bundled ai-robots-txt list, whether that bot may crawl the current page path. If AI crawlers are blocked they cannot fetch the page, so it cannot be cited or used by AI search and assistants.

scoring.summary: Site check at path /. No robots.txt: 8/12 (inconclusive when it is generated at build time). Empty robots.txt: 12. Otherwise each bot in references/ai-bots.json is tested with the RFC 9309 parser. The 10 major bots share 9 points and the other 116 share 3; blocking any major bot caps the score at 9; any allowed bot with Crawl-delay over 5s costs 2. Status follows the shared 80% / 50% rule.

rules.condition: no robots.txt in the served root and no robots.txt generator
rules.message: robots.txt not found - all bots allowed by default

rules.condition: Generated robots.txt (no file in the served root, but src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk/robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, or a CMS in report-only mode)
robots.txt body is empty after trim()

parser (lib/robots.mjs, RFC 9309): '#' comments stripped; consecutive User-agent lines form one group sharing its rules; user-agent tokens match case-insensitively; a bot with its own group ignores the * group
path match: the longest matching Allow/Disallow pattern wins, Allow wins a tie; '*' matches any sequence, trailing '$' anchors; empty Disallow ignored; path tested is '/'
crawl delay: the largest Crawl-delay among the groups that apply to the bot (no inheritance of the * delay by bots with their own group); only counted for allowed bots
base score
rules.points: Math.round(9 * majorAllowed / 10 + 3 * otherAllowed / 116), where the 10 major bots are listed in references/ai-bots.json (major_bots)

rules.condition: any major bot blocked
one or more allowed bots have crawl-delay > 5
findings
rules.note: one finding per blocking robots.txt rule (file + line, first 5 bots named) and one per Crawl-delay group over 5s

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: Only when robots.txt is generated (endpoint, framework route, plugin, CMS virtual file) and not present in the served root: 8/12 with inconclusive true. An absent robots.txt in the served root is an informative absence (it will 404 on a static host).

detect.source_procedure: 1) Read robots.txt from the served root (build output, else the source public dir, else the repo root). 2) If absent: if a generator exists (src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk, robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, CMS) report 8 inconclusive, else 8 absent. 3) If whitespace-only: 12. 4) Otherwise parse with lib/robots.mjs and evaluate all 126 names from references/ai-bots.json at '/'. 5) Compute round(allowed/126*12), minus 2 if any allowed bot's effective crawl-delay > 5.

parity.note: Full parity for a static robots.txt, except the RFC 9309 fixes listed in divergences. Differences: host-generated or CDN-managed robots.txt (Cloudflare managed robots.txt, rewrites, WordPress virtual robots.txt) is invisible in source; generated robots.txt is reported inconclusive; the site is evaluated at '/' only, so Disallow rules that target specific page paths are not scored.

checks.fix_summary: Create or edit robots.txt so AI crawlers are allowed (e.g. remove 'Disallow: /' under AI bot groups, avoid Crawl-delay > 5), or add an empty/permissive 'User-agent: *\nAllow: /' file. Place it at public/robots.txt (Vite, Next.js, Astro), static/robots.txt (Hugo), a passthrough file (Eleventy) or site root (static HTML); for Next.js app/robots.ts edit the rules array. Write one User-agent line per group to avoid the extension's grouping bug.

divergences.plugin: Consecutive User-agent lines form one group that shares the rules (lib/robots.mjs).
divergences.reason: RFC 9309; the extension undercounted blocked bots in grouped records.

divergences.extension: Bot names match robots.txt tokens case-sensitively ('gptbot' does not match 'GPTBot').
divergences.plugin: Case-insensitive product-token match.
divergences.reason: RFC 9309; crawlers match case-insensitively.

divergences.extension: Any matching Allow beats any matching Disallow.
divergences.plugin: Longest matching rule wins, Allow wins ties.
divergences.reason: RFC 9309 and Google behaviour; 'Allow: /blog' no longer unblocks '/'.

divergences.extension: The * group's Crawl-delay applies to bots that have their own group.
divergences.plugin: Only the Crawl-delay of the groups that apply to the bot counts.
divergences.reason: A bot with its own group ignores the * group.

divergences.extension: Inline comments ('Disallow: /x # note') become part of the pattern.
divergences.plugin: Comments are stripped before parsing.

divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule (e.g. 2 of 126 blocked still rounds to 12 and passes, with findings).
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

divergences.plugin: Site check at '/', robots.txt read from the served root; a generated robots.txt is inconclusive instead of absent.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: the repo has no request path, and a generator's output cannot be read without building.

divergences.extension: All 126 bots count equally: score = round(allowed / 126 * 12), so blocking GPTBot and ClaudeBot still scores 12/12.
divergences.plugin: Ten major AI search and assistant crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended) share 9 points and the other 116 share 3: score = round(9 * majorAllowed / 10 + 3 * otherAllowed / 116). divergences.reason: Blocking the crawlers behind ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Apple Intelligence is what actually removes a site from AI answers; an obscure scraper should not weigh the same.

checks.name: llms.txt Detection
checks.description: Checks for an /llms.txt file at the site root (llmstxt.org proposal), that it is non-trivial, not blocked by robots.txt, and follows the spec shape (H1 title plus markdown links). llms.txt gives AI assistants and agents a curated, navigable index of the site's key content. /llms-full.txt is detected but not scored.

scoring.summary: llms.txt absent from the served root -> 0. Generated llms.txt that cannot be read -> 3 (inconclusive). Otherwise start at 5: empty file -3, else < 50 characters -1; blocked for User-agent * by robots.txt (lib/robots.mjs longest match) -2; +1 if the format is valid (first non-empty line '# Title' AND at least one markdown link). Clamp 0..6. llms-full.txt is reported, not scored.

rules.condition: no llms.txt in the served root and no generator
no llms.txt file but a generator exists (src/pages/llms.txt.*, app/llms.txt/route.*, layouts/index.llms.txt, llms.txt templates, a package with 'llms' in its name, or a CMS in report-only mode)
start
file length (JS string length) === 0
else file length < 50
robots.txt in the served root blocks '/llms.txt' for User-agent: * (canCrawl(parsed, '*', '/llms.txt'): longest match wins, Allow wins ties, comments stripped)
file length > 10000
hasH1 = first non-empty line (trimmed) matches /^#\s+\S/ ; linkCount = matches of /\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]+\)/g ; valid = hasH1 AND linkCount > 0. hasSummary and sectionCount are informational.
format valid
format invalid and file non-empty
score = max(0, min(6, score))
llms-full.txt present in the served root
rules.note: details.llmsFullTxt; recommendation suggests adding it when absent

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning. Typical: valid 6 pass; no H1/links 5 pass; blocked 3-4 warning; empty 2 fail; absent 0 fail.
scoring.inconclusive: Only when llms.txt is generated and not present in the served root: 3/6 with inconclusive true.

detect.source_procedure: 1) Read llms.txt from the served root. 2) If absent: generator present -> 3 inconclusive, else 0. 3) Length 0 -> -3, < 50 -> -1. 4) If robots.txt exists, test '/llms.txt' for User-agent * with lib/robots.mjs -> -2 if blocked (a generated robots.txt is not penalized). 5) First non-empty line '# X' and at least one [text](url) link -> +1. 6) Clamp 0..6. 7) Report whether llms-full.txt exists (no score).

parity.note: Hosts can serve a 200 HTML fallback for unknown paths (SPA rewrites in _redirects, vercel.json, netlify.toml): the extension would then count /llms.txt as found with base 5 (pass) even though no file exists; source analysis should report absent. Conversely, WAF/bot protection returning 403 makes the extension fail where source shows the file. Generated llms.txt (endpoints, plugins, CMS) must be rendered to measure. Cloudflare-managed or CDN-level robots.txt changes are not visible in source.

checks.fix_summary: Generate an llms.txt at the public root (public/ for Astro/Next/Vite, static/ for Hugo, passthrough for Eleventy, repo root for static sites) with '# Site Name', a '> summary' line and '## Section' lists of [Title](url): description links built from the sitemap/pages; optionally also llms-full.txt. Ensure robots.txt does not Disallow /llms.txt for User-agent: *.

divergences.extension: robots.txt block test uses Allow-first precedence, '?' as a wildcard, and last-User-agent-only grouping.
divergences.plugin: lib/robots.mjs: longest match wins, Allow wins ties, '?' is literal, grouped User-agent lines share rules, comments stripped.
divergences.reason: RFC 9309 (same parser fixes as ai-access.bot-crawlability).

divergences.extension: Status: >= 5 pass, >= 2 warning, else fail (an empty file scores 2 warning).
divergences.plugin: Status derived from the integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule (2/6 is fail, 3/6 warning).
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

divergences.extension: Fetches /llms.txt live; any non-2xx (including 403/429/503/timeout) is fail 0; an HTML soft-200 page counts as found.
divergences.plugin: Reads llms.txt from the served root; absence is informative (0); a generated llms.txt is inconclusive at 3.
divergences.reason: Source vs live, and the unreachable-vs-absent rule.

checks.name: Content Signals
checks.description: Checks whether the site declares Content Signals (search, ai-input, ai-train = yes/no) in robots.txt or in a Content-Signal response header. robots.txt only says whether a crawler may fetch; Content Signals state what AI companies may do with the content (index it, ground answers on it, train on it).
inputs: HTTP response headers of the page (plain GET)
HTTP response headers of the page requested with Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9
AI bot list: keys of src/data/robots.json (ai-robots-txt project)

scoring.summary: Parse Content-Signal lines in robots.txt (served root) and a Content-Signal header from host config for '/' (_headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml). At least one valid key=yes|no pair in either -> 3 (predicted when it comes only from the header). Else, if robots.txt is generated and cannot be read -> 2 inconclusive. Else if robots.txt has a User-agent line naming any AI bot -> 1. Else 0.

rules.condition: Content-Signal directives from lib/robots.mjs parseRobots (anywhere in the file, independent of User-agent groups; '#' comments stripped). Later lines override earlier keys.
split on ','; each part split on '='; key trimmed/lowercased must be one of [search, ai-input, ai-train]; value trimmed/lowercased must be exactly 'yes' or 'no'. Other pairs ignored.
content-signal from site.host.headersFor('/') (first rule with a valid pair). Parsed with the same value parser.
combined = {...headerSignals, ...robotsSignals} (robots wins on conflicts). source = both | robots | header.
at least one valid signal parsed from robots.txt or header
rules.note: predicted: true when the only source is host header config

rules.condition: no valid signals, no robots.txt file, and Generated robots.txt (no file in the served root, but src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk/robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, or a CMS in report-only mode)
no valid signals, and a robots.txt User-agent token (lowercased, comments stripped) equals a name in references/ai-bots.json (case-insensitive)
otherwise (including no robots.txt)

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: Only when robots.txt is generated and not in the served root and no header signal is configured: 2/3, inconclusive true (the extension's value for its all-unreachable branch).

detect.source_procedure: 1) Read robots.txt from the served root and extract Content-Signal lines with lib/robots.mjs. 2) Read a Content-Signal header for '/' from _headers, vercel.json headers or netlify.toml [[headers]] (site.host.headersFor). 3) Any valid pair -> 3. 4) Else a generated robots.txt -> 2 inconclusive. 5) Else User-agent lines naming an AI bot -> 1. 6) Else 0.
detect.llm_criteria: Only for generated robots.txt or header code paths (template logic, env-dependent output): decide what literal robots.txt text and response headers production would emit, then apply the rules mechanically.

parity.note: Hosts and CDNs can add robots.txt content or the Content-Signal header outside the repo (notably Cloudflare managed robots.txt, which injects Content-Signal lines, and Cloudflare Markdown for Agents which sets the header on markdown responses). Generated robots.txt may depend on env vars. The unreachable branch cannot be reproduced from source.

checks.fix_summary: Add a line such as 'Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no' to robots.txt (public/robots.txt for Astro/Next/Vite, static/robots.txt for Hugo, root or passthrough for static/Eleventy, or the generator for app/robots.ts and Hugo robots templates). The yes/no values are a policy choice, so the plugin should propose defaults and let the user confirm; optionally also add a Content-Signal header via _headers, netlify.toml or vercel.json.

divergences.extension: Signals come from live robots.txt, the page response header and the Accept: text/markdown response header; all three unreachable -> 2 inconclusive.
divergences.plugin: robots.txt from the served root and the header from host config for '/'; the Markdown response header (set by CDNs such as Cloudflare) cannot be seen. A generated robots.txt is the inconclusive (2) case; a header-only pass is marked predicted.
divergences.reason: Source vs live.

divergences.extension: A Content-Signal value with a trailing '# comment' is invalid, and 'User-agent: GPTBot # note' does not count as addressing the bot.
divergences.plugin: Comments are stripped before parsing (lib/robots.mjs).
divergences.reason: robots.txt comment syntax; the extension missed valid declarations.

divergences.extension: If robots.txt alone is unreachable but the page responded without a header, the check fails with 0.
divergences.plugin: No equivalent: a robots.txt that exists in the repo is always read; only a generated one is inconclusive.
divergences.reason: Unreachable-vs-absent rule.

checks.name: Indexability
checks.description: Checks the page-level signals that decide whether search and AI engines may index it: the canonical link, meta robots / bot-specific meta noindex, nofollow or none directives, and a soft-404 heuristic. A page that is noindexed, canonicalized to another domain or looks like an error page will not be surfaced or cited by AI search.
inputs: page HTML <head>: meta[name="robots"] and any meta whose name contains 'bot' (case-insensitive)
rendered visible text of main content and of body (innerText)
host config X-Robots-Tag for the page path (_headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml via site.host.headersFor)

scoring.summary: Three sub-checks run first. If any critical issue exists (noindex/none in a robots or *bot* meta tag or in a configured X-Robots-Tag header, a soft 404, or a canonical on a different hostname when the site base URL is known) the score is 0. Otherwise score = 8 minus the canonical penalty (none or no valid href 1, multiple 3, different URL on same host 2, self-referencing 0) minus 2 if any nofollow/none directive exists, floored at 0. Directives are whole comma/space-separated tokens. A result that depends on an X-Robots-Tag header is marked predicted.

rules.condition: canonical: no link[rel="canonical"], or exactly one with an empty/unparseable href
canonical: more than one link[rel="canonical"]

canonical: exactly one, site base URL known (or the href is relative), and the resolved canonical hostname !== the page URL hostname (www vs apex counts as different). Without a base URL an absolute canonical's host is not compared.
rules.message: Canonical points to different domain (critical issue)

rules.condition: canonical: exactly one, same hostname (or host not compared), and either normalizeUrl(canonical) === normalizeUrl(page URL) (protocol//hostname+pathname+search, strip ONE trailing '/', lowercase), or the canonical path resolves (exact, .html, /index.html) to this same file with the same protocol and query. Without a base URL only pathname+search are compared.
canonical: exactly one, same hostname, not self-referencing (different path/file, query, or http vs https)

noindex: any meta[name*="bot" i] (robots, googlebot, GPTBot, ...) or X-Robots-Tag header rule for the page path (also the path without .html) has a directive token 'noindex' or 'none'. Tokens are split on ',' and whitespace; 'max-snippet:', 'max-image-preview:', 'max-video-preview:', 'unavailable_after:' parameters are ignored and a 'ua:' prefix is stripped
nofollow: same sources, directive token 'nofollow' or 'none' (and no noindex, otherwise critical already)

soft404 signal A: document.title lowercased contains a standalone '404' (not inside a phone number or product code), 'not found', 'page not found', the whole word 'error', 'no encontrado' or 'nicht gefunden'

soft404 signal B: word count of main content < 200. Main content = innerText of first match of 'main, article, [role="main"], .content, #content'; fallback body innerText with nav, footer, header, aside, script, style, noscript removed. Words = split on /\s+/
soft404 signal C: first 1000 chars of body visible text (lowercased, whitespace collapsed) contain 'page not found' or a standalone '404'
soft404: 2 or more of signals A/B/C
no critical issue

scoring.status_mapping: Any critical issue: 0 fail. Otherwise from the integer score with the shared rule: 7-8 pass, 4-6 warning, 0-3 fail. Reachable non-critical outcomes: 8, 7 (no canonical), 6 (other URL, or nofollow), 5 (multiple canonicals or no canonical + nofollow), 4, 3.
scoring.inconclusive: Never inconclusive. Results that depend on an X-Robots-Tag rule from host config are marked predicted: verify the live response header.

detect.source_procedure: Per page template/route: 1) Canonical: find <link rel="canonical"> in static *.html; Astro layouts (often href={Astro.url} or new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)); Hugo baseof/head partials ({{ .Permalink }}) plus baseURL in hugo.toml; Eleventy _includes layouts with page.url and site url data; Next.js app router metadata.alternates.canonical (and metadataBase) in app/**/layout.tsx/page.tsx, pages router next/head; Vite SPA index.html. Count occurrences in the composed head (layout + page + SEO components; plugins like @astrojs/sitemap do not add canonicals but next-seo/astro-seo do). Compare the resolved host with the production host (from site/baseURL/metadataBase/vercel or netlify config/CNAME); treat www vs apex mismatch as critical. 2) Robots meta: grep for <meta name="robots"|googlebot|bingbot|...bot> and Next.js metadata.robots ({index:false} renders noindex, {follow:false} renders nofollow); flag directive tokens noindex, none, nofollow (not substrings, so max-image-preview:none is fine). Watch for env-conditional noindex (e.g. noindex on preview builds) and note it. 3) Soft 404: compute title keywords and approximate main-content word count from built HTML (main/article/[role=main]/.content/#content, else body minus nav/footer/header/aside/script/style/noscript), and check the first 1000 chars of visible body text for '404' or 'page not found'. Best done on build output; otherwise let a model estimate word count from template + content files.
detect.llm_criteria: Only for soft-404 when output HTML is unavailable: estimate whether the visible main content of the page has fewer than 200 words, whether the <title> contains a standalone 404, not found, the word error, no encontrado or nicht gefunden, and whether the first ~1000 characters of visible body text contain a standalone '404' or 'page not found' (a 404 inside a phone number or product code does not count). Soft 404 = at least 2 of the 3.

parity.note: Canonical and meta robots are usually exact from templates or metadata exports, but host resolution depends on the production domain, and values injected by JS (SPA route changes, SEO plugins, tag managers) or CMS are invisible in source. Extension compares canonical against the actual visited URL (including http/https, query strings and trailing slash rules), which source can only approximate. Soft-404 depends on rendered innerText and word counts, which source can only estimate without a build. The extension cannot read X-Robots-Tag here; the plugin reads it from host config (_headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml) and marks such results predicted.

checks.fix_summary: Emit exactly one self-referencing absolute canonical per page on the production host (Astro layout <link rel="canonical" href={new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)}>, Hugo {{ .Permalink }}, Eleventy site.url + page.url, Next.js metadataBase + alternates.canonical), and remove noindex/nofollow/none from production robots meta (Next.js metadata.robots). Soft-404 fixes (thin content, error words in titles) need user content and are assisted.

divergences.extension: Directives are substring matches, so 'max-image-preview:none' reads as 'none' and zeroes the check.
divergences.plugin: Directives are whole tokens split on ',' and whitespace; max-* and unavailable_after parameters are skipped and a 'googlebot:' style prefix is stripped.
divergences.reason: False positive on a valid, non-blocking directive.

divergences.extension: Soft-404 signals match '404' anywhere (phone numbers like 404-555-0100, product codes) and 'error' as a substring.
divergences.plugin: '404' must stand alone (not adjacent to letters, digits or hyphens) and 'error' must be a whole word.
divergences.reason: False positives on normal content zeroed the whole check.

divergences.extension: X-Robots-Tag cannot be read from the content script and is ignored.
divergences.plugin: X-Robots-Tag rules from host config for the page path (and its clean URL without .html) count like robots meta; the result is marked predicted.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: a noindex header configured in the repo blocks indexing just like the meta tag; the live header should be verified.

divergences.extension: The canonical is compared with the visited URL; a different hostname is always critical.
divergences.plugin: The page URL is site.baseUrl + page path. When no base URL is known, an absolute canonical's host is not compared and only its path and query are.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: without a base URL the page host is a placeholder, and comparing it would zero every page.

divergences.extension: A canonical to the clean URL (/about) while visiting /about.html is 'different URL' (-2), because the visited URL differs.
divergences.plugin: A canonical whose path a static host would serve from this same file (exact, .html, /index.html) counts as self-referencing, provided protocol and query match.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: the repo file path is not the served URL; clean URLs are the normal way these files are served.

divergences.extension: A canonical link with an empty or invalid href throws (new URL('')).
divergences.plugin: It is treated like a missing canonical (-1) with a finding.

divergences.extension: Status: >= 6 pass, >= 4 warning.

checks.name: Sitemap Detection
checks.description: Probes common sitemap locations at the site root, checks that the sitemap contains URLs and that robots.txt declares a Sitemap. Sitemaps let AI crawlers and search engines discover and refresh all pages rather than relying on link crawling.
inputs: GET {origin}/sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /sitemap-index.xml, /sitemap1.xml (sequential, first response.ok wins, no timeout)

scoring.summary: Look for sitemap.xml, sitemap_index.xml, sitemap-index.xml, sitemap1.xml in the served root (in that order), then any sitemap declared by a robots.txt Sitemap: line that exists on disk. Else a sitemap generator in config (Astro @astrojs/sitemap with site, Hugo default, Next app/sitemap.*, next-sitemap, Eleventy sitemap templates, vite-plugin-sitemap, WordPress core) counts as found (predicted, URL count assumed > 0). None -> 0. Otherwise start at 5: -1 if robots.txt is absent, -2 if robots.txt has no Sitemap: directive (so an absent robots.txt costs 3), -2 if the sitemap has zero <loc> entries. A generated robots.txt is not penalized (inconclusive). Clamp at 0.

rules.condition: no sitemap file at the four probed names, none declared in robots.txt on disk, and no generator
no file but a generator is configured
no robots.txt in the served root and no robots.txt generator
robots.txt absent, or parseRobots(robots).sitemaps is empty (a real 'Sitemap:' directive; commented lines do not count)
count of /<loc[\s>]/ in the sitemap body == 0
body matches /<sitemapindex[\s>]/i
rules.note: informational; child sitemaps are not read

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning. Scores: 5 pass, 3 warning, 2 or less fail.
scoring.inconclusive: When robots.txt is generated (not in the served root): the robots presence and reference penalties are skipped and inconclusive is true.

detect.source_procedure: 1) Probe the served root for sitemap.xml, sitemap_index.xml, sitemap-index.xml, sitemap1.xml, then robots.txt Sitemap: paths that exist on disk. 2) If none, detect a generator (lib/sources.mjs sitemapGenerator) -> predicted found. 3) If still none -> 0. 4) robots.txt absent -1; no Sitemap: directive -2 (skipped if robots.txt is generated). 5) Zero <loc> entries -2.
detect.llm_criteria: Model judges whether a generator config will actually emit a file at one of the four probed paths (e.g. Astro sitemap without site config, conditional Next.js sitemap routes, Hugo disableKinds) and whether the generated sitemap would contain at least one URL.

parity.note: Static files give full parity. Divergence: generated sitemaps depend on build config; hosting may add, rewrite or block routes (WAF/bot protection returning 403 makes the extension report no sitemap); a CMS or server may serve a sitemap not present in the repo; a SPA fallback that returns index.html with 200 for /sitemap.xml counts as "found" in the extension but with 0 <loc> (score 3 or lower); robots.txt may be generated by the host (e.g. Cloudflare managed robots.txt) and differ from the repo.

checks.fix_summary: Add a sitemap at /sitemap.xml or /sitemap-index.xml (Astro @astrojs/sitemap plus site in astro.config, Hugo default sitemap, Next.js app/sitemap.ts, Eleventy sitemap template, public/sitemap.xml for Vite/static) and add "Sitemap: https://<domain>/sitemap.xml" to robots.txt (public/robots.txt, static/robots.txt, app/robots.ts). Requires knowing the production domain.

divergences.extension: Only the four fixed paths are probed; a sitemap declared in robots.txt at another path is 'not found' (fail 0).
divergences.plugin: A sitemap declared by a robots.txt Sitemap: line that exists in the served root also counts.
divergences.reason: Sitemap: in robots.txt is the standard discovery mechanism; the extension produced a false negative.

divergences.plugin: Only a real Sitemap: directive (lib/robots.mjs, comments stripped) counts.

divergences.reason: Source vs live and the unreachable-vs-absent rule.

checks.name: SSL / HTTPS
checks.description: Checks that the page is served over HTTPS and flags mixed content (http: images, scripts, stylesheets, iframes). HTTPS is a basic trust signal for search and AI platforms, and mixed content can be blocked by browsers or agents.
inputs: rendered DOM: img[src], script[src], link[rel="stylesheet"][href], iframe[src]

scoring.summary: Site check. The scheme is inferred (predicted), since the repo cannot show TLS: host config forcing HTTPS (Strict-Transport-Security header rule, or an http:// -> https:// redirect rule) -> https; else the declared site URL (base URL, else canonical / og:url on pages; localhost ignored) -> http or https, except that an http declaration on a host that serves HTTPS by default (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare, GitHub Pages, Firebase) is https; else a known HTTPS host -> https; else unknown. http -> 0. https -> 2, or 1 if any page has mixed content. Unknown -> 1 inconclusive.

rules.condition: inferred scheme is http (declared http:// site URL, nothing forcing HTTPS, host unknown)
no site URL, no canonical/og:url, no HSTS/redirect rule, unknown host
any page matches img[src^="http:"], script[src^="http:"], link[rel="stylesheet"][href^="http:"], iframe[src^="http:"] (case-sensitive prefix, exact rel)
https inferred and no mixed content
canonical or og:url declares http://
rules.note: finding only when the scheme is https by other evidence

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: When nothing in the repo indicates the production scheme: 1/2 with inconclusive true. Every other result is predicted.

detect.source_procedure: 1) HTTPS evidence: Strict-Transport-Security in host header config for '/', http:// -> https:// rules in _redirects / netlify.toml / vercel.json / firebase.json (forced https). 2) Declared site URL: site.baseUrl (CLI --base-url, home canonical/og:url, sitemap <loc>, CNAME, Hugo baseURL, Astro site), and canonical/og:url on every page (http:// ones become findings). 3) Host defaults from config files (netlify.toml, vercel.json, wrangler.*, firebase.json, CNAME, _headers/_redirects). 4) Mixed content: the four extension selectors over every loaded page, one finding per element. 5) Score: http 0; https 2 (1 with mixed content); unknown 1 inconclusive.
detect.llm_criteria: Model decides the production scheme when config is ambiguous (e.g. no site URL, custom domain on a known host) and whether an http: asset reference is actually rendered on the page (not in comments, docs code blocks or dead components).

parity.note: The protocol is a property of the deployment, not the repo; the plugin infers it from host config, declared URLs and host defaults and marks the result predicted. Mixed content from built HTML matches the extension, but scripts injected at runtime and CMS content are not visible. Protocol-relative (//) and uppercase (HTTP:) URLs are not flagged, as in the extension.

checks.fix_summary: Rewrite http:// asset URLs in templates/content to https:// (auto-fixable when the asset is available over HTTPS) and set the site URL config to https (astro site, Hugo baseURL, Next metadataBase). Enabling HTTPS itself (certificate, forced redirect) is host config and report-only unless the host is file-configured (e.g. netlify.toml redirect, vercel defaults).

divergences.extension: Uses the protocol of the live page URL.
divergences.plugin: Infers the scheme from HSTS / http->https redirect rules, the declared site URL (base URL, canonical, og:url) and host defaults; unknown is 1/2 inconclusive.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: TLS is not visible in the repo.

divergences.extension: Mixed content is checked on the current page only.
divergences.plugin: Site check over every loaded page; any mixed content on any page costs the 0.5 point, one finding per element.
divergences.reason: Site-level audit of all pages; findings group by message across pages.

checks.name: HTTP Behavior
checks.description: Probes a random non-existent URL to verify the site returns a real 404/410 (not a soft 404), verifies the current page returns HTTP 200 to a plain fetch, and checks that no X-Robots-Tag response header contains noindex or none. Agents rely on status codes and headers to know whether a fetch succeeded and whether content may be used.
inputs: HTTP GET of a random probe URL: <origin>/aeo-checker-404-probe-<8 random base36 chars> (2500 ms timeout, redirects followed)
HTTP GET of the current page (shared AnalysisContext page response, 3000 ms timeout, redirects followed)
HTTP response header X-Robots-Tag of the current page

scoring.summary: Site check, all predicted from the repo. Three criteria, 1 point each, summed and floored. Unknown URL: 1 if a catch-all rule serves a 404/410, or a 404 page exists (served-root 404.html or framework 404 source) or the stack/host returns 404 by default (Next.js, Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages, Firebase) and no catch-all rewrite (200) or redirect-to-a-page rule covers unknown paths; 0 when such a catch-all exists (soft 404); 0.5 inconclusive when there is no 404 page and the host is unknown or Cloudflare Pages. Page status: fraction of pages not hit by a Basic-Auth header rule, an error-status rule, or a forced redirect to a path with no file. X-Robots-Tag: fraction of pages whose header rules (_headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml, .htaccess) have no value matching /\b(noindex|none)\b/i.

rules.condition: catch-all rule (/*, **, /(.*), /:path*) in _redirects, netlify.toml, vercel.json rewrites/redirects/routes or firebase.json with status 404/410
catch-all rule rewriting (200) or redirecting (3xx) every unknown URL to a fixed page; path-preserving targets (:splat, $1, :path) ignored
no catch-all; 404.html in the served root, or a framework 404 source (src/pages/404.astro, layouts/404.html, app/not-found.*, pages/404.*, public/404.html, static/404.html, 404.md/njk/liquid)
no 404 page, stack is Next.js or host is Netlify / Vercel / GitHub Pages / Firebase (default 404 page with status 404)
no 404 page, host unknown or Cloudflare Pages (SPA fallback with 200 when no 404.html)

page status, per page (or '/' without built pages): Basic-Auth header rule -> 401; rule with status >= 400 matching the path -> that status; forced 3xx redirect (_redirects '!', netlify.toml force, vercel/firebase redirects) to a local path with no file -> 404; unforced _redirects/netlify.toml rules are shadowed by the existing file; 200 rewrites ignored
X-Robots-Tag, per page: any host header rule or .htaccess 'Header set X-Robots-Tag' value matches /\b(noindex|none)\b/i

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: Only the unknown-URL criterion: no 404 page and an unknown (or Cloudflare Pages) host gives 0.5 of its point and inconclusive true. The whole result is always predicted: true.

detect.source_procedure: Infer the host's behavior from repo config; mark as 'predicted' since the real answer needs a live server. 1) 404 handling: look for a custom 404 page and whether the host serves it with status 404: static/Vite: 404.html in public/ or output root (Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, Vercel static all serve 404.html with 404); Astro: src/pages/404.astro; Hugo: layouts/404.html; Eleventy: 404.html/404.md permalink; Next.js: app/not-found.tsx or pages/404.tsx (Next returns 404 by default). Then look for SPA catch-alls that turn unknown URLs into 200: Netlify/Cloudflare _redirects '/* /index.html 200', netlify.toml [[redirects]] from='/*' to='/index.html' status=200, vercel.json rewrites {source:'/(.*)', destination:'/index.html'}, Cloudflare Pages projects WITHOUT a 404.html (Pages then serves index.html as SPA fallback with 200), Firebase hosting rewrites '**', Next.js catch-all routes app/[...slug]/page.tsx that never call notFound(). Also catch-all redirects of unknown paths to '/' (301/302 to a 200 page = soft 404). 2) Page status: check the audited route exists as a page/file and is not redirected or behind auth (middleware.ts, _redirects, vercel.json redirects, netlify.toml redirects, basic-auth headers). 3) X-Robots-Tag: grep _headers (Netlify/Cloudflare Pages), netlify.toml [[headers]], vercel.json headers, next.config.js headers(), Next.js middleware setting X-Robots-Tag, Hugo/server configs (nginx.conf, .htaccess Header set X-Robots-Tag) for values matching /\b(noindex|none)\b/i on paths covering production pages. Note that Vercel adds 'X-Robots-Tag: noindex' automatically on preview deployments only, not production.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge from the repo's hosting target and framework defaults whether (a) a request for a random nonexistent path would return 404/410 or 200 (SPA fallback, catch-all rewrite, redirect to home), (b) the audited page returns 200, and (c) any header rule applying to production pages sets X-Robots-Tag containing noindex or none as a whole word. Award points exactly as the rules say. If the host cannot be identified, report the probe criterion as unknown rather than guessing.

parity.note: The extension observes live HTTP responses; the repo only lets us predict them. Host defaults (Cloudflare Pages SPA fallback when no 404.html exists, framework adapters, CDN or WAF rules, origin servers not in the repo), dashboard-configured headers/redirects, and edge middleware can all differ from what the source shows. The extension also awards points for WAF blocks and timeouts, which source analysis cannot reproduce.

checks.fix_summary: Add a real 404 page (public/404.html, src/pages/404.astro, layouts/404.html, app/not-found.tsx) and remove SPA catch-all 200 rewrites or redirect-to-home rules for unknown paths in _redirects, netlify.toml or vercel.json (or make the catch-all route call notFound()). Remove X-Robots-Tag noindex/none rules for production paths from _headers, netlify.toml [[headers]], vercel.json headers or next.config.js headers(). Host dashboard settings may still need manual changes.

divergences.extension: Probes a random URL, fetches the page and reads its X-Robots-Tag header live.
divergences.plugin: Predicts all three from host config (redirect/rewrite rules, header rules, .htaccess), 404 pages and host defaults; result is predicted.
divergences.reason: Source vs live.

divergences.extension: Unreachable probe or page (0/403/429/503/timeout, any 5xx for the probe) earns the full point with no inconclusive flag.
divergences.plugin: The only unknown case (no 404 page, host unknown) earns half the point with inconclusive true.
divergences.reason: Unreachable-vs-absent rule in the project CLAUDE.md (warning at roughly half weight).

divergences.extension: Page status and X-Robots-Tag are judged for the current page only.
divergences.plugin: Judged for every loaded page; each criterion earns the fraction of pages that pass.
divergences.reason: Site check over all pages; a rule covering one path is visible in source.

divergences.extension: An X-Robots-Tag noindex/none header forces status fail regardless of score.
divergences.plugin: The header point is lost; status is derived from the integer score by the shared rule (so 2/3 is a warning).
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree (engine-derived status).

checks.name: Structured Data
checks.description: Detects JSON-LD (and, as a fallback, Microdata/RDFa) on the page and awards tiered points for schema.org types that AI answer engines use most (FAQPage above all, then HowTo/Product/Organization, then Article/VideoObject/Dataset, then BreadcrumbList/ItemList/Person). Machine-readable entities let AI systems extract facts and Q&A pairs without guessing from prose.
inputs: rendered DOM: every <script type="application/ld+json"> element (text content)
rendered DOM: [itemscope] elements and their itemtype attribute (Microdata)

scoring.summary: Page scope, run on every page. If there is no JSON-LD script, no [itemscope] and no [typeof]/[vocab] element the check scores 0. If no JSON-LD block parses (none present, or all broken) but Microdata/RDFa exists, it is a fixed 4. If every block is broken and there is no Microdata/RDFa, 0. If the only JSON-LD is template-built and unparseable from source, 8 (inconclusive). Otherwise points are summed: base 4 (at least one block parses), FAQ 8 valid / 4 only invalid, each Tier 1 type (HowTo, Product, Organization family) 3 / 1, each Tier 2 type (Article family, VideoObject, Dataset) 2 / 0.5, each Tier 3 type (BreadcrumbList, ItemList, Person) 1 / 0. Total = min(15, Math.round(sum)); if template-built blocks could not be parsed and the total is below 8, it is raised to 8 and marked inconclusive. Every typed node at any depth (including @graph and nested objects) counts; a type is valid when at least one of its nodes validates with lib/schema-validator.mjs. Status comes from the engine (>= 12 pass, >= 8 warning).

rules.condition: count(script[type="application/ld+json"]) == 0 AND count([itemscope]) == 0 AND count([typeof]) == 0 AND count([vocab]) == 0
no JSON-LD block parses (zero blocks, or every block has invalid JSON) AND (Microdata found OR RDFa found)
rules.note: Fixed 4 regardless of Microdata/RDFa types or validity. Microdata types = itemtype matched by /schema\.org\/(\w+)/ (else raw itemtype). RDFa types = typeof split on whitespace. RDFa 'found' needs [typeof] or [vocab]; [property] alone (e.g. OpenGraph meta property=) does NOT count.

rules.condition: JSON-LD present: parse each script textContent with JSON.parse (template tags substituted first, see divergences); parse failures are reported as findings
base: at least one JSON-LD block parsed successfully
FAQ: any entity with @type 'FAQPage' (string or inside @type array); valid if SchemaValidator.validateFAQPage passes for at least one
Tier 1 HowTo: @type 'HowTo'
Tier 1 Product: @type 'Product'

Tier 1 Organization: @type in ['Organization','LocalBusiness','Restaurant','Store','MedicalBusiness','LegalService','FinancialService','FoodEstablishment','HealthAndBeautyBusiness','HomeAndConstructionBusiness','EntertainmentBusiness','AutomotiveBusiness','Corporation','GovernmentOrganization','EducationalOrganization','MedicalOrganization','NGO','Airline']. Nested objects count too (e.g. Article.publisher of @type Organization).
Tier 2 Article: @type in ['Article','BlogPosting','NewsArticle','TechArticle']
Tier 2 VideoObject: @type 'VideoObject'
Tier 2 Dataset: @type 'Dataset'
Tier 3 BreadcrumbList: @type 'BreadcrumbList'
Tier 3 ItemList: @type 'ItemList'
Tier 3 Person: @type 'Person' (nested author objects count)
any other @type (WebPage, WebSite, Question, Answer, ListItem, ImageObject, etc.)
rules.note: Categorized as Other; contributes nothing. Matching is exact and case-sensitive after stripping a leading http(s)://schema.org/, so 'schema:FAQPage' does not match.

rules.condition: total
rules.points: min(15, Math.round(base + faq + tier1 + tier2 + tier3))

rules.condition: validator FAQPage: mainEntity must be an array (else invalid). Each item: @type === 'Question', has name, has acceptedAnswer with @type === 'Answer' and non-empty text
validator HowTo: name required; step must be an array; HowToSection items are expanded into their itemListElement steps; at least 2 steps; each step @type HowToStep and has text or name
validator Product: name, image, description required; offers required; each offer needs price (0 allowed), priceRange or lowPrice AND priceCurrency; if aggregateRating present it needs ratingValue
validator Organization (all subtypes): only name required (url/logo/sameAs/address/telephone/openingHours are warnings only)

validator Article types: headline required; author required (if first author is an object, after @id resolution, it needs name; a string author is only a warning); datePublished required and must be ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time)
validator Person: name required
validator BreadcrumbList: itemListElement must be an array; each item needs truthy position and name or item.name
validator ItemList: itemListElement must be an array (nothing else required)
validator VideoObject: name, description, thumbnailUrl, uploadDate (ISO 8601) required
validator Dataset: name and description required
JSON-LD only template-built and unparseable from source (no parseable block, no broken block, no Microdata/RDFa)
rules.note: inconclusive; verify on the built or live page

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the integer score: >= 80% (12) pass, >= 50% (8) warning, else fail. Same thresholds as the extension.

detect.source_procedure: Script checks/structured-data/present.mjs runs on every HTML page the site model loads (built output or static HTML). It uses lib/jsonld.mjs extractJsonLd(doc, { templates: true }) to parse blocks (template tags substituted) and collect every typed node, lib/schema-validator.mjs validateNodes to validate them, and [itemscope] / [typeof] / [vocab] for the Microdata/RDFa fallback. For unbuilt framework sources, build first; JSON-LD injected at runtime (tag managers, client-side React) is not visible.

parity.note: Exact when JSON-LD is literal in HTML or when the built output can be scanned. Differs when JSON-LD is assembled at runtime (client-side injection by GTM, Yoast/Rank Math style CMS plugins, React state), built from CMS data or template variables that cannot be resolved statically (validity of name/headline/datePublished then unknown), or injected per-route in SPAs. Extension evaluates one URL; source audit may cover many templates.

checks.fix_summary: Add a JSON-LD <script type="application/ld+json"> block in the shared head/layout (Organization with name/url/logo/sameAs on every page; WebSite) and page-type blocks (Article/BlogPosting with headline, author {Person name}, datePublished; FAQPage only where visible Q&A exists; BreadcrumbList). Goes in index.html / Astro layout / Hugo partial / Eleventy _includes / Next.js layout.tsx or page.tsx. Skeletons can be generated automatically, but real names, FAQ content, prices and dates need user data.

divergences.plugin: Broken JSON-LD does not hide Microdata/RDFa: the fixed 4 applies whenever no JSON-LD block parses.
divergences.reason: Bug: a syntax error in one block wiped out credit for valid Microdata.

divergences.plugin: A leading http(s)://schema.org/ is stripped before matching.
divergences.reason: Full IRIs are valid JSON-LD for the same type.

divergences.extension: isValidISO8601 is new Date(x) not NaN, so strings like "March 3, 2024" pass as ISO 8601.
divergences.plugin: datePublished and uploadDate must have the ISO 8601 shape (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time and zone) and parse as a date.

divergences.plugin: HowToSection steps are accepted and their itemListElement HowToStep items are validated and counted.

divergences.plugin: price 0, lowPrice and ratingValue 0 count as present.
divergences.reason: Free products and AggregateOffer are valid; falsy checks flagged normal content.

divergences.plugin: Validators resolve pure {"@id"} references (also for HowTo step and offers) against any node on the page that defines that @id.
divergences.reason: Same intent (Yoast/Rank Math @graph pattern), applied consistently.

divergences.plugin: Reads HTML from the repo. JSON-LD holding template tags ({{ }}, {% %}, <% %>, <? ?>) is parsed with the tags replaced by a placeholder that counts as a present value; the result is marked predicted. A block that still cannot be parsed is never counted as a JSON error: the check reports inconclusive with partial credit and asks for a build or a live check.

checks.name: Schema Validation
checks.description: Parses every JSON-LD block, resolves @id references, walks every typed node (including nested ones) and validates known types against required-field rules. Broken or incomplete structured data is ignored or misread by AI engines and rich-result parsers, so valid markup is what actually gets used.

scoring.summary: Page scope. No JSON-LD blocks -> 0. Only template-built blocks that cannot be parsed from source -> 3, inconclusive. Otherwise start at 5; subtract 0.5 per block that fails JSON.parse; compute validationRate = round(100 * valid / validatable) over every typed node (nested included, each node once, typed references to a node defined on the page skipped) whose type has a validator; if no validatable node exists the rate is 100, but if no block parsed at all the rate is 0. Subtract 2 if rate < 50, 1 if rate < 80, 0.5 if rate < 100. Clamp at 0, round to 1 decimal; the engine floors to an integer. If template-built blocks could not be parsed and the score is below 3 it is raised to 3 (inconclusive).

rules.condition: zero script[type="application/ld+json"] elements
each block where JSON.parse(textContent) throws (after template-tag substitution; template-built blocks that still fail are not counted, see divergences)

validators resolve pure {"@id": X} references (mainEntity, acceptedAnswer, author, step, itemListElement, offers) against any node on the page that defines X; a typed node whose @id is defined more fully elsewhere on the page is a reference and is not validated on its own

every object with @type anywhere in a parsed block (top level, @graph items, nested objects and arrays), each object once by identity; an @type array yields one entry per distinct validator (e.g. Organization + LocalBusiness validates once)
validationRate < 50
rules.issue: Only N% of schemas pass validation

rules.condition: 50 <= validationRate < 80
80 <= validationRate < 100
validationRate == 100 (including when no node has a validator, as long as at least one block parsed)
score = floor(max(0, round(score*10)/10))
rules.examples: one parse error only -> 4; rate 80-99 -> 4; rate 50-79 -> 4; rate < 50 -> 3; rate < 50 plus 1 parse error -> 2; 2 parse errors -> 4; 3 parse errors -> 3; a single broken block and nothing else -> 2

rules.condition: Each rule below is an ISSUE (makes node invalid). Warnings never affect score. Types not listed return valid: null and are excluded from the rate (e.g. WebSite, WebPage, ImageObject, Offer, Question, Answer, HowToStep, ListItem, PostalAddress, SearchAction, Recipe, Event, Review, Dentist and any other LocalBusiness subtype not listed). Types are matched after stripping a leading http(s)://schema.org/.
node @type in: FAQPage. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: mainEntity missing or not an array (stops)

issues: step missing or not an array (stops)
step missing both text and name

rules.condition: node @type in: Product. Any issue makes the node invalid
issues: each offer (array or single) missing price (0 allowed), priceRange and lowPrice
aggregateRating present but missing ratingValue (0 allowed)

Any issue makes the node invalid

datePublished not ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time and zone)

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the integer score: >= 80% (4-5) pass, >= 50% (3) warning, else fail. A single parse error with everything else valid is therefore pass (4), where the extension said warning.

detect.source_procedure: Script checks/structured-data/valid.mjs runs on every HTML page the site model loads (built output or static HTML), using lib/jsonld.mjs extractJsonLd(doc, { templates: true }) and lib/schema-validator.mjs (a port of the extension's SchemaValidator) validateNodes. For unbuilt framework sources, build first; runtime-injected JSON-LD is not visible.

parity.note: Full parity when JSON-LD is literal in templates or a build output is available. Partial when JSON-LD is assembled at runtime (SPA frameworks, tag managers, CMS plugins injecting JSON-LD), when values come from CMS/frontmatter (a missing headline or datePublished depends on per-post data), or when templates emit different blocks per page type. Template syntax inside literal blocks can make static JSON.parse fail where the rendered page parses fine, so template tags must be substituted before parsing, never counted as parse errors.

checks.fix_summary: Fix JSON syntax and add missing required properties per validator (e.g. Organization.name, Article headline/author{name}/datePublished ISO date, Product name/image/description/offers{price,priceCurrency}, FAQPage Question/acceptedAnswer Answer text, BreadcrumbList position/name) in the JSON-LD source: layout templates, Astro/Next components, Hugo partials, Eleventy includes or index.html. Values drawn from existing page data; content like prices or answer text may need the user.

divergences.extension: If every block fails JSON.parse, validationRate defaults to 100, so only the 0.5-per-block penalty applies (one broken block alone scores 4).
divergences.plugin: If no block parses, validationRate is 0 (one broken block alone scores 2).
divergences.reason: Bug: a page whose only structured data is broken passed validation.

divergences.extension: After @id resolution a @graph node referenced from author/publisher is collected twice (graph item and nested copy), so it counts double in the rate; @type arrays count once per type.
divergences.plugin: Each node is validated once (by identity), once per distinct validator.
divergences.reason: Bug: double counting skewed the rate.

divergences.extension: @type must match exactly, so full IRIs like "https://schema.org/Organization" fall into Other.
divergences.plugin: A leading http(s)://schema.org/ is stripped before matching.
divergences.reason: Full IRIs are valid JSON-LD for the same type.

divergences.extension: isValidISO8601 is new Date(x) not NaN, so strings like "March 3, 2024" pass as ISO 8601.
divergences.plugin: datePublished and uploadDate must have the ISO 8601 shape (YYYY-MM-DD with optional time and zone) and parse as a date.
divergences.reason: The issue text says ISO 8601; the code accepted non-ISO dates (comment/code mismatch).

divergences.extension: HowTo steps must all be @type HowToStep; HowToSection groups make the HowTo invalid.
divergences.plugin: HowToSection steps are accepted and their itemListElement HowToStep items are validated and counted.
divergences.reason: HowToSection is valid schema.org and Google-supported; the extension penalized normal markup.

divergences.extension: Offer price 0 counts as missing (falsy check); AggregateOffer lowPrice is not accepted; aggregateRating ratingValue 0 is missing.
divergences.plugin: price 0, lowPrice and ratingValue 0 count as present.
divergences.reason: Free products and AggregateOffer are valid; falsy checks flagged normal content.

divergences.extension: Only the properties mainEntity, itemListElement, acceptedAnswer, author, publisher have pure {"@id"} references resolved, against @graph items and top-level objects.
divergences.plugin: Validators resolve pure {"@id"} references (also for HowTo step and offers) against any node on the page that defines that @id.
divergences.reason: Same intent (Yoast/Rank Math @graph pattern), applied consistently.

divergences.extension: A typed reference such as publisher {"@type": "Organization", "@id": "#org"} is validated on its own and is invalid for lacking name, even when #org is fully defined on the page.
divergences.plugin: When the same @id is defined more fully elsewhere on the page, the typed reference is not validated separately; the full definition is. Unresolvable references are still validated (extension behaviour).
divergences.reason: False positive on normal @graph markup.

divergences.extension: Status uses validationRate thresholds (pass only at 100% with no parse errors), independent of the score.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

divergences.extension: Reads the rendered page, where template tags are already filled in.
divergences.plugin: Reads HTML from the repo. JSON-LD holding template tags ({{ }}, {% %}, <% %>, <? ?>) is parsed with the tags replaced by a placeholder that counts as a present value; the result is marked predicted. A block that still cannot be parsed is never counted as a JSON error: the check reports inconclusive with partial credit and asks for a build or a live check.
divergences.reason: Source vs live: template values are unknown in the repo, and unrendered syntax is not a real error.

checks.name: Meta Title
checks.description: Checks that the page has a <title>, that it is 50-60 characters, that it is not a generic placeholder like 'Home', that it carries page context beyond a bare brand name, and that it is not stuffed with separators. The title is the primary label AI search and LLMs use to identify and cite a page.
inputs: page HTML <head> <title> (document.title of the rendered page)

scoring.summary: Start at 5. Empty/whitespace title returns fail 0 immediately. Otherwise subtract a length penalty (only one applies), 2 for a generic title, 0.5 for a short (<20 chars) title with no '-', '|' or ':', and 0.5 for more than 3 separator characters. finalScore = max(0, round to 1 decimal). Status uses finalScore; the reported score is Math.floor(finalScore).

rules.condition: document.title trimmed length == 0 (no <title> or empty)
start
trimmed length < 40
40 <= trimmed length < 50
trimmed length > 70
60 < trimmed length <= 70
50 <= trimmed length <= 60
trimmed title matches (case-insensitive, whole string) one of: home, welcome, untitled, new page, page, document, index, test, website, my website, my blog, blog, site, my site, homepage
trimmed length < 20 AND title contains none of '-', '|', ':' (brand-only)
count of characters matching /[-|:]/g in the title > 3 (every hyphen counts, including hyphens inside words)
finalScore

scoring.status_mapping: Uses unfloored finalScore: >= 4 pass, >= 2.5 warning, else fail. Reported points are floored, so e.g. a 45-char title gets finalScore 4.5, status pass, score 4; a title < 20 chars with no separator gets 5-2-0.5 = 2.5, status warning, score 2.

detect.source_procedure: Resolve the <title> each page will render. Static HTML: <title> in each *.html. Vite SPA: index.html <title> (note runtime document.title changes). Astro: <title> in src/layouts/*.astro, usually {title} from props; resolve the value passed from each src/pages/** file (frontmatter or Layout title="..." prop), including any template like `${title} | Site`. Hugo: layouts/_default/baseof.html or partials/head.html <title>{{ .Title }} ...{{ .Site.Title }}</title>; resolve with content front matter title and hugo.toml/config.toml title. Eleventy: _includes/** layouts <title>{{ title }}</title> with front matter/data files. Next.js app router: export const metadata = { title } or generateMetadata in app/**/layout.tsx and page.tsx, including title.template ('%s | Brand') and title.default from the root layout; pages router: <title> inside next/head in pages/** or _app. Best: build and read output HTML. Then apply rules on the trimmed, whitespace-collapsed string (browser document.title collapses internal whitespace and decodes entities).

parity.note: Full when the title is a literal or resolvable from front matter/metadata exports. Differs when titles come from CMS data, i18n, runtime document.title updates in SPAs (react-helmet, vue-meta), or template composition that cannot be evaluated statically. Source audits every page, extension scores just the visited one.

checks.fix_summary: Set a unique 50-60 character title per page in the form 'Page Topic | Brand' using the stack's mechanism (index.html <title>, Astro Layout title prop, Hugo front matter title plus baseof template, Eleventy front matter, Next.js metadata.title with title.template in the root layout). The plugin can fix templates (add a brand suffix, remove duplicate separators) automatically, but page-specific wording needs user review.

divergences.extension: Every hyphen, pipe or colon counts as a separator, including hyphens inside words ("step-by-step").
divergences.plugin: Only standalone separators count: " - ", " | ", " : ", ": ", spaced en/em dashes and middle dots.
divergences.reason: Hyphenated words are not separators; the extension penalized normal English.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded score (4.5 is pass) while the reported score is floored (4).
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

checks.name: Meta Description
checks.description: Checks that the page has a non-empty, well-sized, non-generic <meta name="description"> that is not a copy of the title and not keyword-stuffed. Search engines and LLMs use the description as a compact summary and snippet of the page.

scoring.summary: Start at 5. Missing tag (meta[name="description"], name matched case-insensitively) or empty content => 0. Otherwise deduct for trimmed length (<70 -2; 70-119 -1; >170 -1; 161-170 -0.5; 120-160 none), generic/placeholder opening (-2), exact match with the title (-1) and keyword stuffing (-0.5). Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine; status from the integer score (>= 80% pass, >= 50% warning).

rules.condition: no element matches meta[name="description" i] (first match only; name compared case-insensitively)
content.trim().length === 0
trimmed length < 70
70 <= length < 120
length > 170

trimmed description matches any generic regex (case-insensitive): /^welcome to/, /^this is a/, /^this page/, /^description$/, /^lorem ipsum/, /^todo/, /^placeholder/, /^my website/, /^my blog/, /^my site/, /^about us$/, /^contact us$/, /^contact$/, /^services$/, /^products$/, /^home page/, /^homepage$/, /^default description/, /^add description here/, /^enter description/, /^website description/, /^page description/
description.toLowerCase().trim() === document.title.toLowerCase().trim()
keyword stuffing: split lowercase description on /\s+/, count words with length > 3; max count > 3 AND total word count > 10
CTA regex /\b(learn|discover|find|get|see|read|explore|check|try|start)\b/i
score = max(0, score); the engine floors it to an integer

scoring.status_mapping: From the floored integer score: 4-5 pass, 3 warning, 0-2 fail. E.g. 4.5 => 4 pass, 3.5 => 3 warning, 2.5 => 2 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Find the description meta and title per page. Static HTML / Vite: <meta name="description"> and <title> in each *.html / index.html. Astro: src/layouts/*.astro and page frontmatter props passed to the layout (e.g. description prop) in src/pages/**. Hugo: layouts/_default/baseof.html, layouts/partials/head*.html; value usually from .Description / .Params.description / site.Params.description in hugo.toml/config.toml and content front matter. Eleventy: _includes/** layout plus front matter 'description' in src/**. Next.js app router: export const metadata / generateMetadata in app/**/layout.tsx and page.tsx (description, title, title.template); pages router: <Head> in pages/_app, _document or per page, next-seo configs. Resolve template variables from front matter/config where possible, then apply the rules above with the final string lengths.

parity.note: Exact when the description is a literal in HTML or front matter. Differs when the value is computed at runtime (JS-injected via react-helmet/SPA, CMS-fetched data, generateMetadata with remote data), when a title template suffix changes document.title (affects the title-equality rule), or when a framework adds a default description. HTML entities must be decoded before measuring length.

checks.fix_summary: Add or rewrite <meta name="description" content="..."> with 120-160 characters (ideally 150-160), unique per page, not identical to the title and not starting with generic phrases. Place in the head layout (Astro layout prop, Hugo front matter description, Eleventy front matter, Next.js metadata.description, index.html for Vite); the plugin can draft text from page content but the user should approve it.

divergences.extension: meta[name="description"] is matched case-sensitively, so name="Description" counts as missing.
divergences.plugin: The name attribute is matched case-insensitively.
divergences.reason: Search engines read name="Description"; failing it was a false negative.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded decimal score while the reported score is floored.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

divergences.extension: Reads the rendered DOM of the visited page.
divergences.plugin: Reads each built/static HTML file in the served root, with entities decoded before measuring.
divergences.reason: The plugin audits the repo, not a live page.

checks.name: Open Graph
checks.description: Checks for Open Graph meta tags (og:title, og:description, og:image required; og:url, og:type recommended) and that og:url agrees with the canonical URL. OG tags give social platforms and LLM crawlers a clean, structured summary of the page.

scoring.summary: Tags are read from meta[property="og:X"], falling back to meta[name="og:X"]. Start at 3: -0.75 per missing required tag (og:title, og:description, og:image), -0.75 per present-but-empty required tag, -0.25 if og:url missing, -0.25 if og:type missing, -0.25 if og:url and a canonical both exist and normalizeUrl(og:url) !== normalizeUrl(canonical). A non-absolute og:image is reported but not scored. Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine; status from the integer score.

rules.condition: getMetaContent(p) = content of meta[property="p"], else of meta[name="p"]; null if neither element exists
each of og:title, og:description, og:image missing (null)
each of og:title, og:description, og:image present but content.trim() empty
og:url missing (null)
og:type missing (null)
og:image truthy but new URL(og:image) throws (relative URL such as '/img.png')

og:url truthy AND link[rel="canonical"] has an href AND normalizeUrl(og:url) !== normalizeUrl(canonical). normalizeUrl = protocol//hostname + pathname + search, trailing '/' removed, lowercased. A relative canonical is resolved against the page URL (site base URL + path); when no base URL is known it is resolved against og:url instead.
og:site_name, og:locale
score = max(0, score); the engine floors it to an integer

scoring.status_mapping: From the floored integer score: 3 pass, 2 warning, 0-1 fail. Examples: all present and consistent => 3 pass; missing og:url or og:type or mismatch => 2 warning; one required missing => 2 warning; nothing at all => 0 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Per page, collect og:* meta tags and the canonical link. Static HTML / Vite: *.html, index.html. Astro: layouts/SEO components (astro-seo openGraph prop, custom Head.astro). Hugo: layouts/partials/head*.html, {{ template "_internal/opengraph.html" . }} (emits og:title, og:description, og:type, og:url, og:image when images/params set) and canonical from .Permalink; baseURL from hugo.toml. Eleventy: _includes/** layouts. Next.js app router: metadata.openGraph {title, description, images, url, type} and metadata.alternates.canonical plus metadataBase in app/**/layout.tsx|page.tsx; pages router: <Head> or next-seo. Resolve template values to strings (use site base URL from config to absolutize canonical), then apply rules.

parity.note: Exact for literal tags. Differs for runtime-injected tags, framework or plugin defaults not visible in source (Hugo internal templates, Next.js metadata merging and metadataBase absolutization), template values empty at build time, and og:url vs canonical comparison when either depends on deployment base URL or trailing-slash settings of the host.

checks.fix_summary: Add og:title, og:description, og:image (absolute URL), og:url (equal to the canonical) and og:type (website or article) as <meta property=...> in the shared head layout, or via Next.js metadata.openGraph, Hugo _internal/opengraph.html with images params, Astro/Eleventy layout head.

divergences.extension: Only meta[property="og:*"] is read; name="og:*" counts as missing.
divergences.plugin: name="og:*" is accepted as a fallback when no property= tag exists.
divergences.reason: Consumers accept both and the extension's Twitter check already reads both; failing it was a false negative.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded decimal score while the reported score is floored.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

divergences.extension: The canonical href is resolved by the browser against the visited URL.
divergences.plugin: A relative canonical is resolved against the page URL built from site.baseUrl; without a base URL it is resolved against og:url.
divergences.reason: Source substitute: there is no visited URL, and resolving against a placeholder host would always mismatch.

checks.name: Twitter Cards
checks.description: Checks for Twitter/X Card meta tags (twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image) with a valid card type, giving partial credit when only Open Graph tags exist. These tags control link previews on X and are extra structured metadata LLMs can read.

scoring.summary: Tags are read with meta[name="twitter:X"] falling back to meta[property="twitter:X"]. If none of twitter:card/title/description/image exist but any og:title/og:description/og:image (property= or name=) has non-empty content, score 2. Otherwise start at 3: -0.75 per missing required tag (card, title, description), -0.75 per present-but-empty required tag, -0.5 if twitter:image missing, -0.25 if twitter:card value not in [summary, summary_large_image, app, player]. Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine; status from the integer score.

rules.condition: getMetaContent(name): document.querySelector('meta[name="'+name+'"]') || document.querySelector('meta[property="'+name+'"]'); returns its content or null if no element
twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image all null AND (og:title || og:description || og:image content truthy, read from property= or name=)
each required tag (card, title, description) missing (null)
each required tag present but content.trim() empty
twitter:image missing (null); empty twitter:image is NOT penalized
twitter:card truthy and not one of ['summary', 'summary_large_image', 'app', 'player'] (exact, case-sensitive)
twitter:site and twitter:creator
score = max(0, score); the engine floors it to an integer

scoring.status_mapping: From the floored integer score: 3 pass, 2 warning, 0-1 fail. Examples: all 4 tags valid => 3 pass; only image missing => 2 warning; invalid card type => 2 warning; one required missing => 2 warning (1 fail if image also missing); OG-only => 2 warning; nothing => 0 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Per page, collect twitter:* and og:* meta tags from the head. Static HTML / Vite: *.html, index.html. Astro: src/layouts/*.astro, SEO components (e.g. astro-seo props twitter={...}), src/components/**/Head*.astro. Hugo: layouts/partials/head*.html, including internal templates {{ template "_internal/twitter_cards.html" . }} and "_internal/opengraph.html" (these emit twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, and twitter:image when images configured). Eleventy: _includes/** layouts. Next.js app router: metadata.twitter {card, title, description, images} and metadata.openGraph in app/**/layout.tsx|page.tsx (Next emits name="twitter:*"; whether Next.js derives twitter tags from openGraph depends on version, so inspect the build output if unsure); pages router: <Head> tags, next-seo DefaultSeo twitter config. Apply the rules above.

parity.note: Exact for literal tags. Differs for tags injected at runtime (react-helmet in SPAs), SEO plugins/framework defaults that emit tags not visible in source (Hugo internal templates, Next.js metadata merging, Astro SEO integrations), and template values that may render empty at build time.

checks.fix_summary: Add <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">, twitter:title, twitter:description and twitter:image to the shared head layout, populated from the same variables as the page title/description/OG image (Next.js metadata.twitter, Hugo _internal/twitter_cards.html, Astro/Eleventy layout head).

divergences.extension: The OG fallback only looks at meta[property="og:*"].
divergences.plugin: The OG fallback also accepts meta[name="og:*"].
divergences.reason: Kept consistent with meta.open-graph, which accepts name= as a fallback.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded decimal score while the reported score is floored.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score by the shared 80% / 50% rule.
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

checks.name: Language Tags
checks.description: Checks that <html> has a lang attribute in the simple 'll' or 'll-RR' form using a recognised language (and region) code; hreflang and Content-Language meta are recorded. Language declaration helps LLMs and search engines interpret and route content to the right locale.

scoring.summary: Start at 3. Missing or whitespace-only lang: -2. If present it must match language[-Script][-REGION] (/^([a-z]{2,3})(-[a-z]{4})?(-([a-z]{2}|\d{3}))?$/i) else -0.5; if it matches but the language code is neither in the extension's 70-code list nor known to the runtime's ICU data (Intl.DisplayNames), -0.5; else if a region is present and is neither numeric (UN M.49), in the 70-region list, nor known to ICU, -0.25. hreflang and Content-Language are informational (finding only, no points). Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine.

rules.condition: html lang attribute missing or trim() empty
lang.trim() does not match /^([a-z]{2,3})(?:-([a-z]{4}))?(?:-([a-z]{2}|\d{3}))?$/i (e.g. 'en_US', 'en-US-x-foo' fail; 'zh-Hans', 'zh-Hant-TW', 'es-419' pass)

language code (lowercased) not in the extension list (en es fr de it pt ru ja ko zh ar hi bn pa te mr ta ur gu kn nl pl uk ro el hu cs sv da fi no nb nn tr th vi id ms he fa sw tl fil ca eu gl sr hr bs sk sl bg mk sq et lv lt mt is ga cy af zu xh am ne si km lo my) AND Intl.DisplayNames has no English name for it

else region present (uppercased), not a 3-digit UN M.49 code, not in the extension list (US GB CA AU NZ IE ZA IN PK NG ES MX AR CO PE VE CL EC GT CU FR BE CH LU MC DE AT IT PT BR RU UA BY KZ JP KR CN TW HK SG NL PL RO GR HU CZ SE DK FI NO TR TH VN ID MY PH IL AE SA EG KE GH MA DZ TN LY ET TZ UG ZW) AND Intl.DisplayNames has no name for it
more than 1 link[hreflang] and none has hreflang exactly 'x-default'
meta[http-equiv="Content-Language"] content
score = max(0, score); the engine floors it to an integer

scoring.status_mapping: From the floored integer score: 3 pass, 2 warning, 0-1 fail. Valid lang => 3 pass; unknown region, bad format or unknown language => 2 warning; missing lang => 1 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Find the root <html> tag per page. Static HTML / Vite: <html lang> in *.html / index.html. Astro: <html lang=...> in src/layouts/*.astro (may be a variable such as Astro.currentLocale). Hugo: layouts/_default/baseof.html, typically lang="{{ .Site.LanguageCode }}" or {{ site.Language.LanguageCode }}; resolve from languageCode / defaultContentLanguage in hugo.toml/config.toml (Hugo languageCode like 'en-us' passes: regex is case-insensitive and region is uppercased). Eleventy: base layout in _includes/**, lang from _data/site.* or front matter. Next.js app router: <html lang> in app/layout.tsx (or app/[locale]/layout.tsx); pages router: <Html lang> in pages/_document.tsx, or i18n.defaultLocale in next.config.js (Next adds lang automatically when i18n is configured). Resolve the value and apply the rules; collect <link rel=alternate hreflang> for informational output.

parity.note: Exact for literal lang values. Differs when lang is a template variable resolved at build/runtime, set by client-side i18n libraries after load, or added by a framework automatically (Next.js i18n). hreflang has no score impact so mismatches there do not matter.

checks.fix_summary: Set <html lang="en"> (or the correct 'll' / 'll-RR' code such as en-US) in the root layout: index.html, Astro layout, Hugo baseof.html with languageCode in hugo.toml, Eleventy base layout, Next.js app/layout.tsx or pages/_document.tsx.

divergences.extension: Valid BCP 47 tags with a script subtag or numeric region (zh-Hans, zh-Hant-TW, es-419) fail the format regex (-0.5).
divergences.plugin: language[-Script][-REGION] with a 2-letter or 3-digit region is accepted.
divergences.reason: These are correct language tags; penalizing them was a false positive.

divergences.extension: Only a 70-language and 70-region subset counts as known, so valid codes like 'la', 'eo' or the region in 'lv-LV' are penalized.
divergences.plugin: A code outside those lists still counts as known when the runtime's ICU data (Intl.DisplayNames) has a name for it.
divergences.reason: False positives on valid ISO 639 / ISO 3166 codes.

divergences.extension: Status comes from the unrounded score, so any lang issue shows 'pass' with 2/3 points and 'warning' is unreachable.
divergences.plugin: Status is derived from the reported integer score (2/3 is a warning).
divergences.reason: Status and score must agree.

checks.name: Mobile Friendly
checks.description: Checks the viewport meta tag: present, width=device-width, and initial-scale=1. Mobile-first indexing is standard, and a correct viewport is the baseline signal of a mobile-ready page. It does not test real responsiveness.

scoring.summary: No viewport meta (name matched case-insensitively) => 0. Otherwise start at 3; content is split on ',' or ';' and each part on '=' (trimmed, keys lowercased). width != 'device-width' (case-insensitive): -1.5 if a width value is set, -1 if width absent. initial-scale absent/empty: -0.5; present but parseFloat != 1: -0.25. user-scalable=no/0, maximum-scale < 2 and ';' separators produce findings only. Score = max(0, score), floored by the engine.

rules.condition: no element for meta[name="viewport" i]
settings.width lowercased === 'device-width' (content split on ',' or ';', keys lowercased)
width set to another value (e.g. 1024)
width key absent
initial-scale key absent or empty
initial-scale present and parseFloat(value) !== 1 (e.g. 1.0 is fine, 0.5 not)
user-scalable === 'no' or '0'

Compute percentage and score per rules. Evaluate per page template (home plus a representative content page) and report per page; if a build output exists, parse built HTML instead.
