checks.name: Internal Linking
checks.description: Counts same-host links on the page, separating navigation (nav/header/footer) from in-content links, and penalises generic anchor text such as 'click here' in content. scoring.summary: Start at 4. Internal = a[href] whose href is not mailto:/tel:/javascript:/# and whose resolved http(s) hostname equals the page hostname ignoring a leading 'www.' (page URL from the site base URL; relative links are always internal). 0 internal links -> -3. Else if content links < 3 AND total internal < 5 -> -1. Generic anchor text on content (non-nav) links -> -0.25 each, max -1. Anchor text falls back to aria-label, img alt, then title when the link has no text. link.closest('nav, header, footer, [role="navigation"]') -> nav link; otherwise content link

text = visible text (innerText approximation) trimmed and lowercased, or when empty: aria-label, then the first non-empty img alt, then title; generic if length < 2 or exactly one of: 'click here', 'here', 'read more', 'more', 'link', 'learn more', 'this', 'this link', 'click', 'go', 'see more', 'view', 'details', 'info'
total internal links === 0
else content links < 3 AND total internal links < 5
generic content (non-nav) links count N > 0
descriptivePercentage, uniqueDestinations (distinct pathnames), navToContentRatio: no score effect
score = max(0, round(score*10)/10); the engine floors it

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule on the floored score: 4 pass, 2-3 warning, 0-1 fail.

detect.source_procedure: Runs per page on the built HTML in the served root. Collect a[href], classify internal against the page URL built from the site base URL (www and apex are the same site), mark nav links by ancestor nav/header/footer/[role=navigation], compute anchor text (text, else aria-label / img alt / title) and apply the generic list and the count rules. parity.note: The extension sees the rendered DOM including JS-injected links (menus, related posts widgets, CMS content) and uses innerText (hidden text excluded, CSS text-transform can apply). Link hrefs built from variables or data files need resolution. inputs: rendered DOM body: semantic elements, ARIA roles/attributes, form inputs and labels, skip links

scoring.summary: Start at 4. Deduct 1.75 if no <main> or [role="main"]; 0.75 if no <nav> or [role="navigation"]; 0.75 if fewer than 50% of form fields (input except hidden/submit/button/reset/image, textarea, select) are labelled (only when fields exist); 0.75 if total semantic element count < 5 AND no main. rules.condition: semantic element count = number of elements matching each of: main, nav, article, section, aside, header, footer, figure, figcaption (summed)
no <main> element and no [role="main"]
no <nav> element and no [role="navigation"]

fields = 'input:not([type="hidden" i]), textarea, select' minus inputs of type submit, button, reset or image; a field is labelled if its id equals the for attribute of some <label> (compared as strings), or it has a non-empty aria-label or aria-labelledby, or it is inside a <label>. If fields exist and round(labelled/fields*100) < 50
semanticCount < 5 AND no main (hasMain false)
ARIA counts ([role=main|navigation|banner|contentinfo|search|complementary], [aria-label], [aria-labelledby], [aria-describedby])
skip link: a[href^="#main"], a[href^="#content"], .skip-link, .skip-to-content
score = max(0, round(score*10)/10); the engine floors it

checks.name: Server-Rendered Content
checks.description: Compares the raw HTML the server returns (no JavaScript) with the rendered DOM to see how much of the visible text, the H1 and the title exist before hydration. Most AI crawlers and agents do not execute JavaScript, so client-only content is invisible to them.
inputs: raw HTML of the page via plain GET (status, content-type, body, redirected, truncated)
rendered DOM: document.body text, first <h1>, document.title

scoring.summary: The built HTML in the repo is what a non-JS agent receives, so it is evaluated on its own (no rendered-DOM comparison). Count words in the body (textContent without script, style, noscript, template, svg). Look for an empty SPA mount (#root, #app, #__next, #__nuxt, #___gatsby, #svelte, #q-app, [data-reactroot]; any matching element). Empty mount and < 50 words -> 0. Empty mount and 50-149 words -> 3 (predicted). No empty mount, < 30 words and client scripts -> 3 (inconclusive). Otherwise 6. On a page flagged by one of those rules, -1 if the HTML has no <h1> and -1 if it has no <title> (floor 0).

rules.condition: body textContent without script, style, noscript, template, svg subtrees, split on /\s+/
<script> with no type or type module / text/javascript / application/javascript, having src or inline code
first selector in ['#root', '#app', '#__next', '#__nuxt', '#___gatsby', '#svelte', '#q-app', '[data-reactroot]'] with ANY matching element whose textContent.trim() is empty
empty app root AND words < 50
empty app root AND 50 <= words < 150
no empty app root AND words < 30 AND client scripts present
otherwise (server HTML carries the content)
one of the three rules above fired AND the HTML has no <h1>
one of the three rules above fired AND the HTML <title> is empty or missing
score = max(0, score)

scoring.status_mapping: Engine rule: 5-6 pass, 3-4 warning, 0-2 fail; inconclusive results are always warning.
scoring.inconclusive: A near-empty body that loads scripts (no SPA mount found) scores 3 with inconclusive true: the HTML alone cannot show whether JavaScript adds the content. Verify live with curl -s <url>.

detect.source_procedure: Runs per page on the built HTML in the served root (static HTML, dist/, _site/, public/ after hugo, out/). Parse the HTML, count body words, look for empty SPA mount points and for <h1>/<title>, and score as above. Needs a build for framework sites; Vite SPA output usually has an empty #root/#app and scores 0.
detect.llm_criteria: Decide whether the page's main text, H1 and <title> are emitted in server HTML or only after client JavaScript runs. Estimate the share of final visible words present in server HTML and bucket it: < 25% -> 0, 25-59% -> 3, >= 60% -> 6. Any SPA mount node from the selector list that is empty in server HTML is an automatic 0 (even if other content exists).

parity.note: The extension diffs a live fetch against the live DOM. The plugin only has the built HTML, which is what non-JS agents receive, so it cannot measure how much text client JavaScript adds; it infers JS rendering from empty SPA mounts and near-empty bodies. Middleware, edge rendering, A/B scripts, CMS content, consent walls, bot-specific responses and host behavior (redirects, 404/401, compression) are not visible.

checks.fix_summary: Serve meaningful HTML without JavaScript: use SSR/SSG or prerendering (Astro default output instead of client:only, Next.js server components or getStaticProps instead of useEffect fetching or ssr:false, vite-plugin-ssr/prerender or a static generator for Vite SPAs), and make sure <h1> and <title> are in the server HTML (Next metadata export, Astro/Hugo layouts). These are architectural changes the plugin can outline or partially apply but the user must approve.

divergences.extension: Computes ratio = raw words / rendered-DOM words and buckets it (< 0.25 -> 0, < 0.6 -> 3, else 6).
divergences.plugin: Scores the raw HTML alone: an empty SPA mount with < 50 words -> 0, with 50-149 words -> 3, a near-empty body that loads scripts -> 3 inconclusive, otherwise 6.
divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: the repo has no rendered DOM. The built HTML is what agents receive.

divergences.extension: An empty app root forces 0 even when the rest of the page is fully server-rendered (e.g. an empty widget mount).
divergences.plugin: An empty mount only costs points when the server HTML has little text (< 150 words).
divergences.reason: Server-rendered pages with a small client widget were failed.

divergences.extension: Only the first element per app-root selector is checked.
divergences.plugin: Every matching element is checked.
divergences.reason: A non-empty first [data-reactroot] hid an empty real mount.

divergences.plugin: -1 each when the HTML lacks <h1> / <title> on a page already flagged as client-rendered (predicted).
divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: whether JavaScript adds them cannot be seen; a missing H1 on a static page is the headings check's job.

divergences.extension: Unreachable or non-200 fetches score warning 3; non-HTML content types pass; redirected or truncated fails are raised to 3.
divergences.plugin: Not applicable: only .html files in the served root are audited.
divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: no HTTP fetch.

checks.name: Markdown for Agents
checks.description: Checks whether the page offers a Markdown representation to AI agents: via HTTP content negotiation (Accept: text/markdown), an advertised alternate (<link rel=alternate type=text/markdown> or Link header), or an undiscoverable .md sibling file. Markdown gives agents the same content at a fraction of the tokens of HTML.
inputs: HTTP GET of page with 'Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9' (status, Content-Type, Link, Vary, X-Markdown-Tokens headers)
HTTP GET of .md probe URL (1500 ms timeout)

scoring.summary: Tiered, first match wins: (1) server/edge code or host config in the repo that branches on the Accept header and returns text/markdown -> 5 (predicted); (2) the page has <link rel=alternate type=text/markdown|text/x-markdown> or host config sets a Link header value with both rel=alternate and a markdown type -> 3; (3) a non-HTML .md file for the page exists in the served root -> 2 (predicted); (4) otherwise 0. Every result below 5 is inconclusive: CDN-level negotiation (e.g. Cloudflare Markdown for Agents) cannot be seen in the repo.

rules.condition: md paths: '/' -> '/index.md'; '/x.html' or '/x.htm' -> '/x.md'; '/dir/' -> '/dir.md' and '/dir/index.md'; other last segment with a dot -> none; else path + '.md'

a file among middleware.(js|ts), src/middleware.*, _worker.js, worker.js, src/worker.*, src/index.ts, server.(js|mjs|ts), code under functions/, netlify/edge-functions/, middleware/, src/middleware/, workers/, src/workers/, server/, or vercel.json / netlify.toml / nginx.conf / Caddyfile / wrangler.toml contains 'text/markdown' and the word 'accept' (not Accept-*)

page has link[rel~="alternate"][type="text/markdown"] or [type="text/x-markdown"], OR a Link header value configured for the page path (_headers, netlify.toml, vercel.json) that itself has a markdown type and rel alternate
a file at one of the md paths exists in the served root, its body does not start with <!doctype or <html, and host config does not give it an HTML Content-Type
none of the above

scoring.status_mapping: 5 pass; otherwise inconclusive, so the engine reports warning for 3, 2 and 0.
scoring.inconclusive: Whether the host answers Accept: text/markdown cannot be seen in the repo when it is a CDN setting, so every result below 5 is inconclusive and the finding gives the curl command to verify live. The score still reflects what the repo shows.

detect.source_procedure: Runs per page. Tier 1: scan edge/server code and host config files for Accept-header handling that returns text/markdown. Tier 2: the page's <link rel=alternate type=text/markdown> and Link headers from _headers / netlify.toml / vercel.json for the page path. Tier 3: a .md file for the page path in the served root (see md paths). Static hosts serve .md with a markdown or text Content-Type, so the file content is not required to start with '# '.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge whether any server/edge code or host config found actually returns Content-Type text/markdown when the request Accept header contains text/markdown for the audited page (not just for a single API route). If unsure, do not award tier 1; fall back to tiers 2/3.

parity.note: Content negotiation is a runtime server/CDN property (often a Cloudflare dashboard toggle) and usually invisible in the repo, so source can under-report tier 1. DOM alternate links injected by JavaScript are seen by the extension but not in static templates. The .md probe depends on the host serving .md files with a non-HTML content type and on SPA fallbacks not returning index.html. Unreachable/WAF cases (inconclusive 3) cannot be reproduced from source.

Full 5/5 needs server or edge content negotiation (Cloudflare Markdown for Agents toggle, a Pages/_middleware or Next.js middleware that returns text/markdown for Accept: text/markdown), which the user must enable or approve.

divergences.plugin: Tier 1 looks for Accept handling that returns text/markdown in edge/server code or host config (predicted 5). Results below 5 are marked inconclusive with a curl command to verify.
divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: negotiation is runtime behaviour, often a CDN toggle not in the repo.

divergences.reason: Static sites serve pages as .html, so the probe never ran for them.

divergences.reason: An unrelated rel=alternate next to another link mentioning text/markdown was counted.

divergences.reason: Source-vs-live: static hosts serve .md files with a markdown/text type; the Content-Type is not in the repo.

checks.name: Agent-Usable Controls
checks.description: Checks that interactive controls are operable through the accessibility tree, which is how browsing agents act on a page: buttons have accessible names and are focusable, links have real hrefs, click handlers are not on bare divs/spans, and personal-data inputs declare autocomplete. An icon-only button or an href-less link is invisible as an action to an agent.
inputs: rendered DOM: all <a> elements and their href/aria/name/id/onclick attributes
rendered DOM: div/span/li/p/img/td elements with an inline onclick attribute
rendered DOM: all <input> elements with type, name, id, autocomplete
hidden / aria-hidden="true" attributes on elements and ancestors

scoring.summary: Four categories, 1 point each. Elements inside (or being) [hidden] or [aria-hidden="true"] are ignored. For each category: if it has 0 elements it earns 1 point; otherwise it earns 1 point when Math.round((total - problems) / total * 100) >= 90. If all four categories are empty the check passes with 4 and a 'no interactive controls' message.

rules.condition: buttons: elements = 'button, [role="button"], input[type="submit"], input[type="button"], input[type="reset"], input[type="image"]' not hidden. Problem (max one per element) if no accessible name, OR role="button" on a non-native element (native = button, input, select, textarea, summary, a[href]) without a tabindex attribute
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no buttons

rules.condition: accessible name order: non-blank aria-label; text of elements referenced by aria-labelledby ids; trimmed textContent (includes visually hidden text); title; value attribute; alt attribute; descendant img[alt] with non-blank alt; descendant 'svg > title' text; input type submit/reset with nothing else still counts as named

links: all <a> except role="button" and hidden ones. Problem if href is missing, blank, exactly '#', or starts with 'javascript:' (case-insensitive, trimmed), UNLESS the anchor has aria-haspopup or aria-expanded, OR it is a named anchor (has name or id, has no text content, and has no onclick)
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no links

rules.condition: fakeClickables: 'div[onclick], span[onclick], li[onclick], p[onclick], img[onclick], td[onclick]' whose role is not 'button' (those are in the buttons category) and not hidden. Problem if no tabindex attribute
rules.note: Only literal inline onclick attributes; listeners attached with addEventListener or framework handlers (React onClick, Vue @click, Svelte on:click, Alpine @click) are not visible and never count

rules.condition: autocomplete: <input> elements not hidden. Candidate if type (lowercased, default 'text') is not in ['hidden','password','search','checkbox','radio','submit','button','reset','file','image','range','color'] AND (type is 'email' or 'tel' OR a token of `${name} ${id}` (split on - _ space digits and camelCase, lowercased), or two adjacent tokens joined, is one of fname, firstname, lname, lastname, fullname, surname, name, address, street, city, zip, zipcode, postal, postalcode, postcode, phone, tel, email, country, state, company, organization). Problem if autocomplete attribute is missing, blank, or 'off'
rules.points: +1 if pass rate >= 90% or no candidates

rules.condition: all four categories have total 0

scoring.status_mapping: score 4 pass, 2-3 warning, 0-1 fail.

Per-page percentages depend on how components compose into a page, so component-level source scans can differ from the per-URL result. CSS-hidden elements are counted by both (only hidden/aria-hidden are excluded).

checks.name: Agent Protocol Discovery
checks.description: Checks whether the site publishes machine-readable discovery artifacts (MCP server card, A2A agent card, agent skills index, RFC 9727 API catalog, OpenAPI, OAuth metadata, /.well-known/ai) or declarative WebMCP tool annotations, so AI agents can find and use its tools and APIs without reading docs. Conditional: returns 'na' (removed from the score denominator) when the site shows no API or agent surface.
inputs: HTTP GET of 11 well-known / discovery paths on the page origin (body, status, content-type)
rendered DOM: a[href] (first 500), link[rel~=service-desc|describedby], script[type=application/ld+json], elements with [toolname] or [tooldescription]

scoring.summary: Looks for the 11 discovery files in the served root (and source public dir). A file counts only if its body is not HTML (by host-config Content-Type or leading <!doctype/<html) and the path's validator passes on the parsed JSON. A framework route handler that would serve the path (app/**/route.ts, src/pages/**.ts, src/routes/**/+server.ts) counts as predicted. Found artifacts are grouped into categories (mcp, a2a, skills, api, oauth, ai); WebMCP annotations on any audited page add 'webmcp'. 3+ categories -> 6, 2 -> 5, 1 -> 3. If none: same-site API evidence on any audited page -> 0; else not applicable (na, excluded from the denominator).

rules.condition: for each path, read <servedRoot or fileRoot><path>, then <sourcePublicDir><path>; Content-Type from host config headers for the path (_headers, netlify.toml, vercel.json)
isHtml = /text\/html|application\/xhtml/i on the configured content-type OR body matches /^\s*<(!doctype|html)/i. If body non-empty and not HTML, JSON.parse(body); json = null on parse failure.
artifact found when the file exists AND NOT isHtml AND validator(json, file) is true; predicted when no file exists but a route handler for the path does

rules.validator: json is a non-array object with truthy 'name'

rules.label: Agent card
rules.validator: json is a non-array object with truthy 'name'

rules.validator: json is an object or an array

On every audited page, scan the first 500 a[href]; resolve against the page URL (site base URL or a placeholder host, so relative links are same-site); keep http(s) same-site links (lowercase, strip leading 'www.'; equal, or one endsWith '.'+other). Evidence if the first path segment (lowercased) is one of [api, apis, developer, developers, docs, documentation, graphql, swagger, openapi, api-docs, api-reference] OR the link hostname matches /^(api|apis|developers?|docs)\./i. Up to 5 samples per page.
Also evidence: link[rel~="service-desc"] or link[rel~="describedby"]; a JSON-LD node (any depth) with @type WebAPI
any exception thrown

scoring.status_mapping: 1 category -> 3 (warning); 2 -> 5 (pass); 3+ -> 6 (pass); none found + API evidence -> 0 (fail); none found + no evidence -> na (weight removed from the denominator).
scoring.inconclusive: Not used: files are read from the repo, so the extension's all-probes-unreachable branch cannot occur. Route handlers are marked predicted.

detect.source_procedure: Site scope. Read the 11 paths from the served root / public dir with the validators above, Content-Type from host config; count framework route handlers for those paths as predicted; scan every audited page for WebMCP attributes and, when nothing is found, for same-site API links, service-desc/describedby links and WebAPI JSON-LD. Repo API routes (pages/api, app/api) are not treated as evidence, matching the extension's page-only evidence.
detect.llm_criteria: Judge only for the no-artifact case: does the site have a developer or API surface? Mirror the extension: same-site links to /api, /apis, /developer(s), /docs, /documentation, /graphql, /swagger, /openapi, /api-docs, /api-reference (first segment only) or to api./apis./developer(s)./docs. subdomains; a service-desc/describedby link; a WebAPI JSON-LD entity. Links to third-party APIs or anchor text alone do NOT count. The extension only inspects the analyzed page's links, so for parity evaluate the site's main layout/nav/footer plus the target page.

parity.note: Artifacts can be served dynamically (edge functions, reverse proxies to an API host, framework route handlers) or set by the host, and Content-Type (relevant for api-catalog linkset and HTML detection) is decided by the server. API evidence in the extension is evaluated on the single rendered page, so links injected by JS or present only on other pages differ. WebMCP attributes added at runtime by JS are visible to the extension (rendered DOM) but may not be in source. The 'all probes unreachable' na branch cannot be reproduced from source.

checks.fix_summary: Publish discovery JSON under the public root (public/.well-known/ for Astro/Next/Vite, static/.well-known/ for Hugo, passthrough for Eleventy): e.g. /.well-known/api-catalog linkset (served with Content-Type application/linkset+json via _headers, netlify.toml or vercel.json headers), /.well-known/openapi.json, an MCP server card at /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json, and OAuth metadata if auth is used. Content (endpoints, auth servers, tool list) must come from the user, so the plugin drafts skeletons only; for content-only sites, no fix is needed (na).
